C1.worst_defect: The hero sentence leans on jargon a half-informed visitor has to decode: 'open-source till for Vendure, the open-source headless commerce framework' ("headless" is unexplained, and 'till' is the only word for what the product is), and the first card under 'What it does today' explains idempotency ('Each sale carries its own id, and the Vendure plugin saves that id with the order in one step') rather than a shop owner's benefit.
C1.where: home/desktop/01 (hero paragraph and 'Every sale lands once' card); same on home/phone/01-02

C2.worst_defect: The home comparison table says the demo 'sends ... anonymous usage events to ph.wcpos.com', a different brand's domain that nowhere on the home page is said to belong to VendurePOS's makers. A first-time visitor sees their data going to an unknown third party; even the linked Connect a till section only says it is 'a self-hosted PostHog analytics server', not who WCPOS is.
C2.where: home/desktop/02 'Live demo or your own store' table, row 'Sales reach Vendure, once each, even offline'; home/phone/04

C3.worst_defect: Step 5 of the quick start has a collapsible headed 'If your store already allows vendurepos.vercel.app'. That domain is never introduced anywhere else, so it reads as a leftover from an old deployment and makes a newcomer wonder whether they are on the right URL. Step 9 also asks the reader to parse 'plugin 0.3.0 advertises order.create 1–5, which includes v4'.

C4.worst_defect: The Changelog reads like internal engineering notes, not release notes: '0.3.0 ... order.create v5 custom lines are real order lines on a plugin-owned, disabled 'POS custom item' variant (SKU TALLY-CUSTOM-ITEM ...) (ADR 0005)' and 'Migration TallyPosV51790900000000 adds the v5 custom fields'. The one-line 'In short' summary is the only part a non-maintainer can use.

C5.worst_defect: The hero screenshot of the till is scaled down so far that its cart text ('incl. Reduced DE 7%', 'Order discount', 'Add charge', product prices) is barely legible at 1440 px, so the one image on the page shows little about how the till works. After the two framed cards, 'What it does today' falls back to a plain two-column text list with no visual anchor.
C5.where: home/desktop/01 (hero image and the feature list below it); home.desktop-dark (same)

C6.worst_defect: On the phone, the hero image swaps to the narrow till layout and its frame shows only the search bar, filter chips and two product cards. The cart is hidden behind a 'Cart (3) · €20.09' tab, so the caption 'A sale in progress on the live demo till.' describes something the reader cannot see.

C7.worst_defect: Everything is present and correct (titles, descriptions, og card, JSON-LD, llms.txt, sitemap, search API, a real 404 with status 404). Lighthouse mobile still flags render-blocking requests (est. 150 ms) and 53 KiB of unused JavaScript on /, and LCP is 2.4 s on both / and /docs/quick-start.

overall_worst.defect: The home page tells a first-time visitor the demo sends usage events to 'ph.wcpos.com' without saying who WCPOS is or how it relates to VendurePOS. On a site whose whole pitch is trust (sales land once, data stays in your browser), an unexplained foreign domain receiving data is what makes a newcomer hesitate before clicking 'Live demo'.
overall_worst.where: home/desktop/02 and home/phone/04, 'Live demo or your own store' table, last row
overall_worst.fix: Name the owner in the same cell, e.g. 'anonymous usage events to our own analytics server (ph.wcpos.com, run by WCPOS, the team behind VendurePOS), with no cookie', and add the same clause to Connect a till › Where requests go.
